result.note: Tests PRAHAAR as India's first national counter-terrorism policy and its key design features.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, the Government of India unveiled PRAHAAR. Which of the following best describes it?
options: India's first comprehensive national counter-terrorism policy
India's first comprehensive national cybersecurity strategy
India's first comprehensive national drone regulation policy
India's first comprehensive national maritime security doctrine
questions.explain: PRAHAAR stands for Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism and is India's first comprehensive national counter-terrorism policy. It brings intelligence agencies, police and prosecutors under one coordinated system.
questions.source: India has unveiled PRAHAAR (Policy for Response Against Hostile Activities and Radicalism), its first comprehensive national counter-terrorism policy.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about PRAHAAR, the national counter-terrorism policy unveiled by India in February 2026:
items: Its threat focus on CBRNED risks covers digital threats alongside chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive ones.
Prosecutors are brought into terror cases only after the investigation has been completed.
Real-time intelligence sharing between federal agencies and state police has been made formal policy.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the policy involves prosecutors from the start, so that terror cases survive court scrutiny. PRAHAAR replaces decades of agency-by-agency responses with a single national playbook.
questions.source: Real-time intelligence sharing between federal agencies and state police is now formal policy, not a system that relies on interpersonal ties.
